narratives.title: Q3: CI enforcement changed the conformance curve
narratives.body: Making style validation a blocking merge check (31% → 62% of repos) is what moved conformance, not enrollment: silver pass rate rose from 52% to 71% while enrollment grew more modestly. Teams fix what blocks their merge. Unplanned breaking changes fell from 7 to 4 — the first quarter the trend has pointed the right way.

narratives.title: Q4: close the enforcement gap, then SDK leverage
narratives.body: Target is blocking validation at 80% of repos and silver pass rate at 85%. Once conformance is stable, the leverage story starts: generated SDKs from conformant OpenAPI should pass 60%.

narratives.title: Q3: adoption is no longer the bottleneck — conformance is
narratives.body: OTel adoption reached 82%, but only 61% of instrumented services emit all four Golden Signals. The gap is concentrated in older Java services instrumented before the telemetry profile existed. MTTR improved from 132 to 98 minutes; alert-based detection rose to 67%, which we attribute to the RED dashboard rollout on the payment path.

narratives.title: Q4: auto-instrumentation closes the conformance gap
narratives.body: Rolling auto-instrumentation to the legacy Java fleet should lift Golden Signals conformance past 80% without team-by-team migration work — the same enforcement-beats-enablement lesson the API domain learned this quarter. That is also the move that takes us from AWS Stage 2 toward Stage 3 practice.
